## **ORDER** 

The present Petition has been filed by PRPL, seeking appropriate direction(s) to CTUIL to approve PRPL’s application dated 08.12.2025 seeking change of source, in terms of Regulation 9.3 of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, as amended (“GNA Regulations”). 

**2.** The Petitioner has made the following prayers vide the instant Petition: 

   - _(a) Direct the Respondent, Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (CTUIL) to forthwith approve the PRPL’s application for change of renewable energy source under Regulation 9.3 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, as amended (GNA Regulations); and_ 

   - _(b) Pass such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may consider deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case_ 

**3.** The Petitioner has also sought interim reliefs vide the Petition as below: 

   - _(a) Direct CTUIL to not create any third-party rights or allocate non-solar hour access corresponding to the PRPL’s Connectivity quantum to any other entity, such that PRPL’s application seeking change of source is not rendered infructuous; and_ 

   - _(b) Pass such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may consider deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case_ 

**4.** Petitioner vide affidavit dated 26.05.2026 has submitted that subsequent to the filing of the Petition on 21.02.2026, the Respondent, Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd. (CTUIL), vide its letter dated 30.04.2026, had approved the Petitioner's change of source request made vide its application dated 08.12.2025. Since the change in fuel source application has been approved by CTUIL, the present Petition has become infructuous. Accordingly, the Petitioner, without prejudice to its rights and remedies available under law, seeks leave to withdraw the present Petition. 

**5.** The matter was called for a hearing on 27.05.2026. During the course of the hearing, learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the affidavit dated 26.05.2026 and submitted that the Petitioner has filed an affidavit seeking withdrawal of the Petition. Accordingly, the learned counsel for the Petitioner prayed to pass the order in this regard. 

**6.** Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the CTUIL had no objection in this regard. 

**==> picture [23 x 18] intentionally omitted <==**

**Order in Petition Number 107/MP/2026** 

Page **2** 

**7.** In view of the affidavit filed by the Petitioner and the submissions of learned counsels for the Petitioner and CTUIL made during the hearing of the matter, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present Petition. 

**8.** Petition No. 107/MP/2026 is disposed of in terms of the above

3. The Petition was admitted, and notice was issued to the parties to file reply and rejoinder. Reply to the Petition has been filed by the Respondent BYPL and the Petitioner has filed a rejoinder thereof.

_(e) The Petition is barred by the contract between the parties itself, as also the Doctrine of Past Practice:_ On 11.1.2017, when the Joint Reconciliation Statements were signed, all the payments made by the Respondent were adjusted firstly towards principal amount and thereafter towards LPSC. The Joint Reconciliation Statement is itself a contract between the parties. As such, the appropriation of dues has to be done in accordance with the terms and conditions mutually agreed between the parties under the PPA, read with the contract between the parties in the form of the Joint Reconciliation Statement executed between them. In the present case, DVC and Respondent have specifically agreed to the Joint Reconciliation Statement, which is itself a contract between the parties. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, in a catena of judgments, has held that the conduct of the parties is a relevant factor in the construction of contracts.  Further, DVC itself has admitted the said fact in the instant Petition (Para 30); therefore, DVC is bound by the same and cannot now unilaterally renege on it thereafter.

During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Respondent submitted that the present Petition may be listed, after the pronouncement of the order in Petition Nos. 239/MP/2019, 54/MP/2021 and 135/MP/2022, dealing with similar issues, as in the present Petition. He further submitted that since BRPL and BYPL are sister concerns, the Petitioner may be requested to give an undertaking not to take any coercive action against the Respondent (similar to the undertaking given to BRPL by THDC in Petition No. 54/MP/2021), till a final decision in the aforesaid three Petitions. The learned counsel for the Petitioner, while pointing out that the matter has been heard at length, did not, however, object to the listing of the present Petition, after a final decision of the Commission, in the aforesaid three Petitions. He, however, submitted that no undertaking will be given by the Petitioner, since the Respondent is liable to make the payment, in terms of the orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court.

13. In response, the learned counsel for the Respondent clarified that all payment been made to the Petitioner, in terms of the orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, and there are no outstanding dues. He further submitted that the payment sought by the Petitioner was only on account of the payment appropriation methodology unilaterally adopted by the Petitioner and therefore, the Respondent is not liable for the same. Considering the parties' submissions, the Commission adjourned the hearing. The Commission, however, directed the Petitioner not to take any precipitative action against the Respondent till the next date of hearing.

44. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondent (BYPL). The Respondent has argued that the issue of payment and alleged non-payment owing to inability to pay is pending adjudication before the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _Writ Petition No. 105 of 2014_ and _Contempt Petition No. 141 of 2014_ (tagged matters), and therefore, DVC ought not to have filed the present Petition. It has been further contended that DVC is seeking to overreach the pending proceedings and that the inability to pay arose on account of a non-cost-reflective tariff determined by the DERC. In this regard, we are of the view that the pendency of the aforesaid Writ Petition and Contempt Petition before the Hon’ble Supreme Court does not operate as a bar to the consideration of the present Petition. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, by its orders dated 26.3.2014, 6.5.2014 and 3.7.2014, directed the Respondent to continue to make recurring monthly payment to the generating and transmission companies in accordance with the basis indicated therein and kept all disputes, including those relating to figures, open for determination at a later stage. Although Writ Petition No. 105 of 2014 was disposed of vide Judgment dated 06.08.2025, Contempt Petition No. 141 of 2014 is still pending before the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Further, the Interim Order dated 26.3.2014 passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court is still subsisting due to the pendency of C.A. Nos. 4011 and 4012 of 2014 before the Hon’ble Supreme Court.
